title: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (WHO)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Classify the exposure, wash every wound with soap and water for 15 minutes, and vaccinate Category II and III exposures at once (WHO 1-week ID: 0.1 mL at 2 sites on days 0, 3 and 7). Add RIG (HRIG 20 IU/kg, ERIG 40 IU/kg) or a monoclonal antibody infiltrated into all Category III wounds in unvaccinated patients.

sections.title: Assess the exposure
items: Category I: touching or feeding animals, licks on intact skin. No exposure: wash the skin, no PEP.
Category II: nibbling of uncovered skin, minor scratches or abrasions without bleeding. Wound washing and immediate vaccination.

Category III: single or multiple transdermal bites or scratches, saliva on mucous membranes or broken skin, or direct contact with bats. Wound washing, immediate vaccination and RIG or rabies monoclonal antibody.
Wounds on the head, neck, face, hands or genitals, multiple or deep bites, a sick or unprovoked animal, and immunodeficiency all raise the risk and the urgency.
Only mammals transmit rabies; no human rabies death is known from a rodent bite. Eating meat or drinking milk from a rabid animal does not need PEP (processing its carcass may).

Start PEP whatever the delay since exposure, even months later. PEP can be stopped if a dog, cat or ferret stays healthy for 10 days from the bite, or the animal tests negative in a reliable laboratory.

sections.title: Wound care (every exposure)
items: Wash and flush every wound with copious running water and soap or detergent for 15 minutes as soon as possible; rinse exposed eyes and mucosa thoroughly with water.
Then apply an antiseptic such as povidone-iodine. Discourage home remedies on the wound.
Do not close or tightly bandage the wound. Avoid suturing; if unavoidable, delay it for some hours after RIG or monoclonal antibody infiltration and keep sutures loose and minimal.
Tetanus vaccine (primary course, or a booster if the last dose was over 10 years ago or per national schedule); consider antibiotics for deep or contaminated wounds.

sections.title: Vaccine schedules: never vaccinated
items: WHO preferred, 1-week intradermal (IPC) regimen: 0.1 mL ID at 2 sites (both deltoids, or thighs or suprascapular areas) on days 0, 3 and 7.

Alternatives: 2-week IM regimen, 1 full vial IM on days 0, 3, 7 and once between days 14 and 28 (4-dose Essen); or 3-week IM regimen, 2 vials on day 0 (one in each deltoid) then 1 vial on days 7 and 21 (Zagreb). Earlier WHO IM schedules remain acceptable.
The dose does not change with age or weight. IM: deltoid in adults and children aged 2 years or more, anterolateral thigh under 2 years; never gluteal; never at the RIG site.

Use cell culture or embryonated egg vaccines (potency 2.5 IU or more per vial); any of them can be given ID even if labelled for IM use, where the national regulator allows. Use opened vials within 6 to 8 hours.
Missed or late doses: resume the schedule, do not restart. Change route or product only if unavoidable, continuing with the schedule for the new route.
Never withhold or delay vaccine because RIG is unavailable; give the first dose and refer for RIG.

sections.title: Rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibody (Category III)
items: Indicated for Category III exposures in people never vaccinated, and for Category II and III exposures in immunocompromised people even if previously vaccinated.

Maximum dose: HRIG 20 IU/kg, ERIG 40 IU/kg, single rabies monoclonal antibody 3.33 IU/kg, monoclonal antibody cocktail 40 IU/kg (WHO 2024); follow the product label for monoclonals. WHO encourages monoclonals instead of RIG where available.

Infiltrate as much as is anatomically feasible deep into and around all wounds, avoiding compartment syndrome; dilute with saline for large or multiple wounds. Do not inject the remainder IM at a distant site; fractionate it aseptically for other patients that day.

Exceptions: inject the remainder IM near the presumed site if unseen wounds are likely (for example a young child) or after bat contact; rinse mucosal exposures with RIG; give RIG IM after aerosol exposure.
Give once, with the first vaccine dose or as soon as possible; not after day 7 of vaccination. No skin test before ERIG; observe for 15 to 20 minutes with anaphylaxis treatment ready.
If supply is short, prioritise multiple or deep bites, bites to the head, neck or hands, severe immunodeficiency, a confirmed or probably rabid animal, and bat exposures.

sections.title: Previously vaccinated, immunocompromised and other groups
items: Previously vaccinated (documented PrEP, or at least 2 doses of a cell culture vaccine as PEP): wound care plus 0.1 mL ID at 1 site on days 0 and 3, or 0.1 mL ID at 4 sites on day 0, or 1 vial IM on days 0 and 3. No RIG. Re-exposure within 3 months of a completed PEP: wound care only.

Immunocompromised (including HIV not on ART or with CD4 below 200 cells/mm3, or below 25% in children under 5, chemotherapy): thorough washing, RIG or monoclonal antibody and a complete vaccine course for Category II and III even if previously vaccinated; check neutralising antibody 2 to 4 weeks after starting and seek specialist advice. ID use is acceptable.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, infancy and old age are not contraindications; any WHO regimen can be used. Chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine is not a contraindication to either route.
After RIG, postpone live vaccines for 3 to 4 months if possible.

National schedules differ: India's 2019 guideline uses a 4-visit ID schedule (days 0, 3, 7, 28) and 5-dose IM Essen and does not treat bat exposure as an indication; US ACIP uses 4 IM doses (days 0, 3, 7, 14) with HRIG 20 IU/kg. This protocol follows WHO.

sections.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)
items: Offer to people at high risk: veterinarians and animal handlers, laboratory staff, people in remote highly endemic areas with poor PEP access, and travellers with extensive rural or cave activities.
WHO schedule: 0.1 mL ID at 2 sites on days 0 and 7, or 1 vial IM on days 0 and 7. A single visit gives partial protection only; give the second dose within 1 year.
No routine boosters after a complete primary series; workers at continual or frequent risk need regular serology and a 1-dose booster if neutralising antibody falls below 0.5 IU/mL.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting to see whether the animal dies before starting PEP.
Omitting RIG or monoclonal antibody in Category III, or injecting it into muscle instead of the wounds.
Suturing a bite before infiltration.
Restarting the whole course after a missed dose.
Giving RIG to a previously vaccinated, immunocompetent patient.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, intradermal (1-week IPC)
drugs.dose: 0.1 mL ID at each of 2 sites on days 0, 3 and 7
drugs.notes: WHO preferred PEP regimen. Same dose at all ages.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, intramuscular (2-week, 4-dose Essen)
drugs.dose: 1 full vial IM on days 0, 3, 7 and once between days 14 and 28
drugs.notes: Deltoid; anterolateral thigh under 2 years. Never gluteal.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, intramuscular (3-week Zagreb)
drugs.dose: 2 vials IM on day 0 (both deltoids), then 1 vial on days 7 and 21

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, previously vaccinated
drugs.dose: 0.1 mL ID at 1 site on days 0 and 3, or ID at 4 sites on day 0, or 1 vial IM on days 0 and 3

drugs.name: Human rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG)
drugs.dose: Up to 20 IU/kg, once, infiltrated into and around all wounds
drugs.notes: Category III in the unvaccinated. Not after day 7 of vaccination.

drugs.name: Equine rabies immunoglobulin (ERIG)
drugs.dose: Up to 40 IU/kg, once, infiltrated into and around all wounds
drugs.notes: No skin test; observe 15 to 20 minutes with anaphylaxis treatment ready.

drugs.name: Rabies monoclonal antibody
drugs.dose: Single monoclonal up to 3.33 IU/kg; monoclonal cocktail up to 40 IU/kg; infiltrated as for RIG
drugs.notes: WHO-encouraged alternative to RIG; follow the product label.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, PrEP
drugs.dose: 0.1 mL ID at 2 sites, or 1 vial IM, on days 0 and 7
drugs.notes: Serology-guided boosters only for continual or frequent occupational risk.
